headline: Single-cell profiling maps glial and immune states across neural injury models
label: Neural Injury Single Cell Profiling
summary: Single-cell atlases now resolve injury-responsive glial, neutrophil, and immune states across stroke, spinal cord, and peripheral nerve models.
synthesis: The dominant thread is single-cell transcriptomics resolving immune and glial states after neural injury. StrokeTime integrates 21 mouse stroke scRNA-seq studies (414,359 cells) into a longitudinal atlas of 17 cell classes and 120 transcriptional states. A reanalysis of three public spinal cord injury datasets maps temporal neutrophil-lineage states G0–G5 and inflammatory-to-lipid shifts. A neuroma-induced DRG atlas separates intervention-specific glial and immune programs, while a tissue dissociation study shows that workflow choices alter reactive astrocyte recovery. Adjacent work addresses macrophage complexity, precision nanomedicine for traumatic neural injury, and multi-omics biomarkers for aging-associated nerve repair. What is new is temporal and intervention-resolved profiling of injury-responsive cells, extended to a human forebrain organoid in which microglia mediate CD8+ T cell recruitment in Alzheimer's disease pathology.
